body:
I don't think we should ask JS to change here. So it's a question of whether HTML can change to JS's semantics.

I think this might be a normative change, but probably one we could get away with.

For integers, the algorithms to compare are:

- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-parsing-integers
- https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parseint-string-radix (with radix = 10)

These definitely seem different, including e.g.:

- the definition of white space that is used
- how much leading/trailing garbage is allowed
- ES's algorithm allows implementation-defined results after 20 digits (!)
- ES's algorithm converts the results to floating point using [𝔽](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#%F0%9D%94%BD).

For floats:

- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values
- https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parsefloat-string which quickly delegates to https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-stringnumericvalue
- https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-stringtonumber which does the same

I haven't investigated the differences there.
